name: 28549-chatdecode-gptoss120b-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3, two GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:2).
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=4, bounded at 400 requests / 5400 s safety, warmup the first 20% by completion, so ~320 of the 400 fall in the measured window.
workload: GuideLLM `json_file`, single turn, no prefix_buckets: `configs/data/mtbench-firstturn-80x5.jsonl` -- the 80 MT-Bench first-turn questions (question_id 81-160, all eight categories) cycled 5 times in file order. `request_format: default-template` wraps each row as a user message and applies the target's own chat template with add_generation_prompt=True; output is capped at 256 tokens and stops at EOS (`ignore_eos: false`), greedy, top_p 1.0.
purpose: A general-purpose chat assistant answering single-turn questions with short replies, four concurrent users, on two GPUs.
launch:
model: openai/gpt-oss-20b

# EAGLE-3 speculative decoding with a published EAGLE3 draft head for this target, k = 3.
# `method` and `draft_tensor_parallel_size` are passed explicitly so neither is inferred.
speculative-config: {"method": "eagle3", "model": "nm-testing/gpt-oss-20B.eagle3.unconverted-drafter", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 2}

tensor-parallel-size: 2
max-model-len: 16384
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.80

# HAZARD -- pinned to what a real `vllm serve` resolves to on an 80GB non-A100 card at this engine.
# Left unset, an in-process run resolves a different pair (2048 / 128), which would make the
# scheduler budget rather than the declared load the thing under test. Neither binds here.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

# Against this engine's default of on: the request file is 80 prompts cycled five times, so with
# prefix caching enabled four fifths of the run would prefill out of cache.
enable-prefix-caching: false
